user_input: Compare AA24-109A and AA23-352A: which actors are reported using Mimikatz, and how do their advisory software-to-technique mappings compare? Cite both reports and keep each mapping within its source context.
response:
Rhysida actors use Mimikatz to gain access to victim systems. [E1, E2]
Akira threat actors use Mimikatz to query and retrieve information from Active Directory. [E3, E4]
CISA maps Rhysida's use of AZCopy to T1059.009 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Cloud API. [E1, E5]
CISA maps Akira's use of net group /domain command to T1082 System Information Discovery. [E3, E4]
CISA maps Akira's use of PCHunter64 to T1082 System Information Discovery. [E3, E4]
CISA maps Akira's use of DiskCheck software to T1082 System Information Discovery. [E3, E4]
CISA maps Akira's use of Adfind.exe to T1087.002 Account Discovery: Domain Account. [E3, E4]
CISA maps Akira's use of net Windows command to T1482 Domain Trust Discovery. [E3, E4]

reference: AA24-109A reports Akira threat actors using Mimikatz, with advisory mappings T1003; AA23-352A reports Play ransomware actors using Mimikatz, with advisory mappings T1003. These mappings describe the cited reports and do not establish that every use of the software has these behaviors. Both reports cite the same parent technique, T1003 (OS Credential Dumping), for their reported Mimikatz use.
